title: Number of Excellent Pairs
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers nums and a positive integer k, determine the number of distinct pairs (num1, num2) such that both num1 and num2 are elements of nums, and the sum of the number of set bits in num1 OR num2 and num1 AND num2 is greater than or equal to k.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers nums and a positive integer k, determine the number of distinct pairs (num1, num2) such that both num1 and num2 are elements of nums, and the sum of the number of set bits in num1 OR num2 and num1 AND num2 is greater than or equal to k. Two pairs are considered distinct if they differ in at least one element, and a pair where num1 equals num2 is also counted if num1 appears in nums.
constraints: A pair is ordered and may use the same value twice.
Duplicate occurrences in nums are discarded before forming pairs.
A pair (a,b) is excellent when popcount(a OR b)+popcount(a AND b) is at least k.
hints: Use popcount(a OR b)+popcount(a AND b)=popcount(a)+popcount(b) bit by bit.
Deduplicate nums, then count how many unique values have each popcount.
Sum count[i]*count[j] for every ordered popcount pair with i+j>=k.
The identity reduces excellence to popcount classes, and the double loop retains ordered pairs and self-pairs exactly.
editorial: The identity reduces excellence to popcount classes, and the double loop retains ordered pairs and self-pairs exactly.

tests.explanation: After deduplication, five ordered pairs have combined bit counts at least three.
No pair has enough combined set bits, so the result is zero.
